AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, copied verbatim as that section binds every batch. The sim has no add-to-room phase - creature creation IS construction - so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (lagavulin_matriarch.py:38-44). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set - the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on target is self.player / applier is self.player / card is not None, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire; sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion - the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering - MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) before the subclass applies its powers, but `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: every initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7 NOTE: that rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does NOT hash, exactly as the seam records disclose. Payload and ORDER match: LagavulinMatriarch.cs:109-113 -> Sleep() (:115-128) sets IsAwake=false, then PlatingPower 12, then AsleepPower 3; the sim sets is_awake=False at :39 (before super(), because build_machine's conditional branch closes over it) then applies PlatingPower 12 and AsleepPower 3 at :43-44 in that order. The remainder of Sleep() is a TriggerAnim and the NSleepingVfx spawn, presentation. ESCALATION CHECK: neither power's amount reads max_hp and neither is applied to a creature other than the owner, so section 2's escalation clause does not fire. Clause (c) holds: the initial state is the MoveState SLEEP_MOVE (executed: monster_probes_b03.py lagavulin-wake prints current=SLEEP_MOVE move=SLEEP_MOVE log=['SLEEP_MOVE'] before any wake), so the first roll is monster_state_machine step 30's sticky no-op and the SLEEP_BRANCH condition is never evaluated before AsleepPower exists.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: LagavulinMatriarch.cs:160-182 vs lagavulin_matriarch.py:46-73, node for node (executed: monster_probes_b03.py graphs). SLEEP_MOVE (SleepIntent) -> SLEEP_BRANCH; SLASH -> DISEMBOWEL -> SLASH2 -> SOUL_SIPHON -> SLASH; initial state SLEEP_MOVE. The only branch is a ConditionalBranchState, and its two AddState calls are in the same ORDER with the same predicates: (:173) SLEEP_MOVE if Creature.HasPower<AsleepPower>(), (:174) SLASH_MOVE if !HasPower<AsleepPower>() -> (py :64-65) `'asleep' in self.powers` / `'asleep' not in self.powers`. Order is observable: ConditionalBranchState.GetNextState returns the FIRST branch that evaluates > 0 (monster_state_machine step 26) and both sides raise if none does. No RandomBranchState anywhere, so PROMPT.md class 6 cannot apply and no roll draws. Intents: SleepIntent -> SLEEP, SingleAttackIntent(19) -> ATTACK 19, MultiAttackIntent(9,2) -> ATTACK 9x2, SingleAttackIntent(12)+DefendIntent -> ATTACK 12 / DEFEND, DebuffIntent+BuffIntent -> DEBUFF / BUFF.

guards.what: wake_up(stunned=...) - the ported half of the AsleepPower wake
guards.rationale: This is the mechanical behaviour the two C# hook overrides do NOT contain. Executed with `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b03.py lagavulin-wake`. DAMAGE WAKE - game (AsleepPower.cs:21-36): remove Plating, IsAwake=true, CreatureCmd.Stun(owner, WakeUpMove, 'SLASH_MOVE'), remove AsleepPower; Creature.StunInternal (Creature.cs:524-544) then builds a synthetic MoveState('STUNNED', WakeUpMove, StunIntent) with FollowUpStateId='SLASH_MOVE' and MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning, so the boss spends one turn on a move whose whole body is an animation and IsAwake=true (LagavulinMatriarch.cs:189-199, mechanically a no-op) and then performs SLASH. Sim (lagavulin_matriarch.py:75-87): is_awake=True, force_current_state(SLASH_MOVE), _current_move=SLASH_MOVE, CreatureCmd.stun(self); combat.py:313-329 skips that turn and clears the flag, and the next turn performs SLASH. Observed after the wake: current=SLASH_MOVE move=SLASH_MOVE stunned=True is_awake=True. Same telegraph (Intent(STUN) while stunned, state_machine.py:315-318), same skipped turn, same next move, and no draw on either side because MoveState.get_next_state is deterministic. NATURAL WAKE - game: AsleepPower.AfterSideTurnEnd decrements to 0 and calls WakeUpMove directly (AsleepPower.cs:46-57), leaving the machine parked on SLEEP_MOVE; the next roll walks SLEEP_BRANCH, finds AsleepPower gone and lands on SLASH_MOVE. Sim: powers.py:1859-1866 expires the power and calls wake_up(stunned=False), which force-sets SLASH directly; observed current=SLASH_MOVE move=SLASH_MOVE stunned=False. Same next move. The `if self.is_awake: return` re-entry guard (py:79-80) mirrors WakeUpMove's own `if (!_isAwake)` (cs:191) plus the PowerCmd.Remove(this) that stops the C# damage path firing twice.
